About this Role  AMI believes AI agents should predict and plan using an internal model of the world — their world model. We’re looking for new team members to advance the state-of-the-art in world modeling. We believe that video is a rich and abundant source of data reflecting how the world works, and that in general models need to be able to process continuous, high-dimensional data from a variety of sensors to: (a) understand context about the current state of the physical world, (b) make predictions about how the world will evolve, possibly as a result of actions taken, and (c) plan and adapt sequences of actions to complete complex tasks, possibly in dynamic, complex environments.

You will work with a team on world model research efforts, with a specific focus on 3D geometry of the real world, including::

Self-supervised learning methods to efficiently learn from video and other continuous, high-dimensional signals

New architectures that efficiently learn to predict world dynamics from video and other high-dimensional signals

Scalable algorithms for pre-processing and curating video data

Evaluations for benchmarking world model understanding, prediction, and planning

Efficient algorithms for model-based planning and reasoning

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science or a related field

Proficiency in Python

Ability to design, run, and analyze experiments independently

Understanding of machine learning fundamentals, large-scale training, and accelerator-based (GPU or TPU) compute environments

Deep expertise in at least one of the following: 3D/4D reconstruction, SLAM or SfM, depth and pose estimation, point tracking.

ZEAL Network SE is an international group shaping the future of digital lotteries and dream-driven experiences. As Germany’s leading online lottery provider through LOTTO24 and Tipp24, and a partner of Spain’s ONCE, ZEAL combines innovation, technology, and entertainment to inspire millions of customers. With ventures such as Freiheit+, Traumhausverlosung, Traumautoverlosung and ZEAL Ventures, the company also invests in new business models and emerging e-commerce brands. Driven by a diverse team of 350+ professionals, ZEAL fosters a collaborative, ambitious culture focused on turning dreams into reality.

We are looking for a  Brand Media Manager (f/m/d)  to drive the strategic planning and operational execution of brand media campaigns across our portfolio of brands, leveraging key channels such as TV, Connected TV (CTV), and YouTube to strengthen brand awareness, maximise reach, and support overall business growth.

Your tasks:

Planning, execution, and optimization of integrated media campaigns across various brand media channels, with a focus on digital brand media (CTV, OLV and YouTube).

Continuous analysis and reporting of media campaign performance, including KPIs.

Building and maintaining relationships with media agencies, sales houses, and other partners to optimize media buying and collaborations.

Identifying and evaluating new media channels and opportunities to expand reach and audience targeting.

Close collaboration with the creative team to ensure all media content authentically reflects the brand message and values.

Budget management and ensuring efficient use of funds for maximum results.

Conducting market and competitor analyses to stay informed about current trends and developments and to derive strategic recommendations.

Close collaboration with other departments such as product management, data analytics, and business functions to ensure the media strategy supports the entire customer journey.

What you offer us:

4–5 years of relevant professional experience in brand media management, ideally with a focus on operational management of CTV and YouTube.

Experience in operational steering of campaigns in the Google Ads Manager and on DSPs (Trade Desk, Amazon Ads Agent)

Solid understanding of the German media landscape and its trends, especially in the traditional media sector.

Strong analytical skills for evaluating campaign performance and deriving insights.

Excellent communication and negotiation skills in German and English.

Experience and knowledge of the media landscape in other European countries is an advantage.

Experience in offline media buying is an advantage.

Ability to work in a dynamic environment and manage several projects simultaneously.

Team-oriented mindset with the ability to collaborate effectively with various stakeholders.

Nice-to-Haves:

Experienced with both Corporate and Start-up surroundings

Media agency background

Understanding of marketing channel synergies (ATL + BTL)

jobs.description:
ZEAL Network SE is a dynamic, international group of companies that has been creating exciting and innovative lottery experiences for over 20 years. As Germany’s largest provider of online lotteries through our brands LOTTO24 and Tipp24, and a trusted partner of Spain’s ONCE, the second-largest national lottery, we’re shaping the future of the lottery industry. We are passionate about driving innovation, as demonstrated by our newest brands, Freiheit+ and Traumhausverlosung, which bring fresh and exciting dreams to life. Additionally, through ZEAL Ventures, we invest in inspiring e-commerce start-ups like Omaze and DAYMADE, fueling fresh ideas and opportunities.

Our team of 350+ professionals from diverse backgrounds is united by a visionary mindset, a passion for collaboration, and a commitment to inspire dreams. At ZEAL, we empower our people to think ambitiously and work together toward a shared purpose: helping people imagine and achieve their aspirations.

As a  (Senior) Quality Engineer (f/m/d)  in our Backoffice Team, you will help shape a new internal platform used across ZEAL to support business-critical operational workflows.  You will join a small cross-functional team and have a high level of ownership from the start. The Backoffice integrates with a wide range of backend services and supports workflows that can have financial, operational and compliance impact. Your work will directly influence how confidently and quickly we can deliver new functionality.  This is an  engineering-focused  quality role. You will work directly in the application codebase alongside the engineers and build the tooling, infrastructure and automated feedback loops that help the team ship safely at high speed.

Your tasks:

Shape and continuously improve the quality engineering strategy for the Backoffice application

Design and build automated test infrastructure across unit, integration, API and end-to-end levels with a strong focus on Playwright and TypeScript

Develop reusable test fixtures, test-data seeding, environment tooling, harnesses and abstractions that make realistic and repeatable testing easy.

Build fast automated feedback loops and validation mechanisms that make AI-assisted development safer and more effective.

Design meaningful regression coverage for critical workflows, complex permissions and scenarios with financial, operational or compliance impact

Strengthen CI quality gates and improve test execution so that a green pipeline provides a strong and fast signal that changes are safe to ship.

Investigate defects, flaky tests and systemic quality issues and turn findings into durable engineering improvements.

Triage bug reports together with internal users, reproduce issues and turn findings into clear actions for the team.

Champion a strong quality mindset across the team and challenge workflows and designs from an end-user perspective to identify usability issues and edge cases early.

Foster knowledge sharing and collaboration

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

Build intuitive experiences across insurance, payments, claims, investments and other financial services.

Maintain and evolve BJAK's design system to ensure consistency across products.

Collaborate closely with product managers and engineers to deliver pixel-perfect implementation.

Ensure accessibility, responsiveness and visual consistency across different devices and platforms.

Contribute to improving overall product usability, interaction patterns and visual language.

2–5 years of experience designing digital products, with a strong focus on mobile applications.

jobs.title: Android Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

Role

As an Android Software Engineer, you own the Android client experience, how AI feels, behaves, and performs on mobile devices. This is not a thin client role. You will build a production Android application where AI interactions are core to the product, and performance, reliability, and clarity matter.

Focus

Build and maintain production Android apps using Kotlin.

Integrate AI-powered features (chat, vision, voice, recommendations) via backend APIs.

Design UX patterns for AI interactions, including streaming responses, retries, and partial results.

Optimize performance, memory usage, and responsiveness for AI-heavy flows.

Implement analytics, logging, and feedback capture to support AI evaluation and iteration.

Collaborate closely with backend and ML engineers on API contracts and system behavior.

Ensure app stability, security, and scalability in production environments.

Ideal Experiences

3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

Hands-on experience integrating AI features (e.g. LLM, vision, speech APIs).

Strong understanding of asynchronous programming (Coroutines, Flow).

Familiarity with REST or gRPC APIs and structured data formats.

Strong debugging and performance profiling skills.

Comfort building in environments with latency, partial failure, and non-deterministic behavior.

Experience with MLKit or light on-device inference.

Published production apps on the Google Play Store.

Outcomes

Stable, smooth, and reliable real-world use android applications.

Performance is optimized: responsive, low-latency, and efficient on memory and CPU.

Production issues are detected early, monitored effectively, and resolved with clear root-cause analysis.

Tech Stack

Kotlin / Java

SQL / noSQL

TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning.  Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Knowledge Engine  – Data Infrastructure
jobs.description:
The Knowledge Platform team builds Exa's knowledge engine. We continuously synthesize information from across the web and beyond into one of the world's largest open-domain knowledge graphs, with hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims. The work has two halves: construction pipelines that decide what to trust, and retrieval engines that decide how best to search it. Our goal is to give agents answers to any factual question about the world with unprecedented precision and completeness.  In this role, you'll build the knowledge  construction pipelines : turning everything from a 100k docs/s web crawl to vendor datasets into a graph of what is true about the world, and keeping it correct as data changes.  This is greenfield work with a massive scope. There is no off-the-shelf system for building a model of the world from the open web, so you'll make foundational decisions, from how claims are represented and resolved to how trust is assigned and how the graph evolves over time, that everything built on top of it depends on.

What you'll do

Continuously synthesize  the live web crawl, vendor deliveries and APIs, and other off-the-web sources into one typed graph: extraction that turns pages and records into ontology-shaped claims, each carrying its provenance, timestamp and confidence.

Bring every new source in cleanly:  versioned, append-only history with schema evolution, late-arriving and corrected records, and replayable cursors, so every claim traces back to the exact delivery that produced it.

Decide what to trust:  entity resolution across billions of records (blocking, pairwise scoring, clustering) into canonical people, companies, places and publications, then truth discovery that weighs source reliability, recency and corroboration to reconcile conflicting claims.

Keep that picture current and convergent:  streams arrive continuously, out of order and at very different rates, so the graph is eventually consistent by design. You'll build incremental computation over change data feeds, where each update is a diff of what changed and every job is idempotent and resumable, so the graph converges to the same state however runs interleave, fail or replay, and readers only ever see committed, consistent versions.

Measure precision and completeness:  labeled evals for extraction and resolution, per-source coverage and correctness metrics, and lineage that pinpoints which source or stage broke and why.

What we're looking for

You've built and operated large-scale distributed data pipelines in production over petabytes of structured and unstructured data, with Spark over a lakehouse format (Delta Lake, Iceberg, Hudi).

You understand incremental processing deeply: change data capture, idempotent writes, backfills and reprocessing.

Strong in Python and at least one systems language; you can read and tune Spark query plans.

You obsess over correctness, reliability and data quality as much as scale.

Bonus

Entity resolution, record link

We're expanding rapidly, pioneering a new category, and we achieved our Series F funding in just four years. With a bias for action and a love for being trailblazers, the team at Plume embodies a combination of relentless curiosity and imaginative innovation. We challenge ourselves to think in ways that other companies don't, work to do what should be done (rather than what can), and if we can't do it exceptionally well, we don't do it. Technical Trusted Advisor: Engage with ISPs to deeply understand their technical and business requirements, and then effectively demonstrate how Plume's solutions can meet and exceed those needs.

We moved past that a while ago: AI agents and human experts create, localise, check and refresh content for global B2B brands every day, across markets and languages. The next question is a harder one: not how to make content, but which content a client should make at all. That's where you come in.  As an AI Builder, you work on both sides of that. About half your time goes to bringing new clients live. The rest goes to building the intelligence that tells each client what to make next: where competitors outrank them, which pages are losing ground and need a refresh, which topics are an opening nobody has claimed yet, and whether they show up when people ask ChatGPT or Google instead of searching.  We've built our own CRM; our teams work with agents that do everything from setting up a tailor-made demo for a prospect to preparing sales calls and routing client feedback to the right person, and people across the company build their own tools. If you want to do serious work with AI, this is a good place for it. Everyone here is already building.

What Contentoo does  Most content tools make the client the editor. Most agencies make them the project manager. We'd rather make them the approver: they brief, review, and approve, and we run everything in between, inside their own workflow and tools. That makes us a product with a large service layer, sitting where SaaS, service and AI overlap.  None of that works without good foundations, so that's where we start. Before any agent runs, we capture what makes a client's content theirs: strategy, tone, terminology, compliance rules and hero pieces, per language and market, confirmed by the client. Every agent, expert and signal draws on that brand context. Skip it, and you get generic content, faster.  There's no shortage of software that tells a client what to write. The difference is that we get those foundations right first and then actually do the work. We've been doing that for ten years: 300+ brands, 300,000+ completed projects and 49 languages.

What you'll do  A suite of Workflows already runs in production, from localisation and creation to brand checks and content refresh. Each one combines AI agents with human experts and works from the client's brand context.  In practice, your week splits two ways. Then you make that whole process faster and more automated on our side, so the next client goes live with less hand work. jobs.title: GPU Engineer
jobs.description:
About Kog  At Kog, we're building real-time LLM inference for AI agents.  Coding agents execute sequences of tasks where each step depends on the model's previous response. The faster the model generates tokens, the faster these agents can reason, code, and act.  Our approach is to co-design model architecture, the inference engine, and low-level GPU kernels to minimize generation latency on standard NVIDIA and AMD datacenter GPUs.  We've developed several technologies to make this possible:

Monokernel:  a persistent GPU program that keeps the entire token generation loop on the GPU, avoiding CPU handoffs.

KCCL:  our custom inter-GPU communication layer, designed to minimize latency.

Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP):  a model architecture that overlaps communication with computation and weight loading.

Laneformer 2B:  our code-generation model demonstrating this co-design approach.

Our engineers work directly with GPU hardware, using CUDA, PTX, HIP, and CDNA ISA to optimize execution.  Implementing and optimizing a new AI model for a specific GPU architecture can take months of manual engineering. Meanwhile, new models are constantly being released.  Our goal is to use AI agents to implement and optimize the models we choose on the GPUs we choose, in a fraction of the time required today.  These agents will build on the GPU optimizations and hardware insights our team has developed. They'll explore optimization strategies, generate and modify kernels, verify correctness, benchmark performance on real hardware, and iterate based on the results.  We want to make model porting and GPU optimization much faster and repeatable, allowing Kog to keep pace with the latest AI models rather than spending months adapting each one manually.  This is a major engineering direction we're now developing, and you'll help shape it.  Learn more at  https://blog.kog.ai .

What you'll work on  You'll join our GPU engineering team to tackle challenging performance problems and help build the internal agents that will accelerate this work.

Develop and optimize GPU kernels using C++, CUDA, HIP, and low-level instructions.

Investigate GPU architecture, memory access, synchronization, and execution bottlenecks.

Profile and benchmark workloads to identify and validate performance improvements.

Optimize inference operations and communication across multiple GPUs.

Implement and optimize new AI models on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.

Help build AI agents for GPU engineering , enabling automated code optimization, correctness testing, benchmarking, and iterative improvements.

Take ownership of technical decisions and their implementation.

What we're looking for  We're looking for an experienced GPU Engineer who can contribute quickly and independently to complex performance problems.

Strong hands-on experience developing and optimizing GPU kernels, ideally using CUDA C++ or HIP/ROCm.

Deep understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, parallel execution, and perform

jobs.description:
Canonical  is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

We are hiring an engineering manager to lead the reboot of our Landscape systems management solution for Ubuntu.

Ubuntu is growing rapidly in the enterprise, with estates expanding from cloud, to bare metal servers, to vSphere clusters, and of course desktops and devices. Ubuntu is easy to deploy and configure, one node at a time, but it's difficult to know where you stand on policy and compliance, patch management, or access control across a large estate. Ubuntu used to be under the radar in the enterprise, but it is now becoming an official platform for many companies. Those enterprises very much want a high quality way to manage their Ubuntu estate.

We started work on Landscape many years ago, and the current generation of the service reflects the choices of the day. We now have the opportunity to invest significantly in a team to bring a fresh new vision for large-scale Ubuntu estate management to the project. That doesn't make this a greenfield opportunity - we have a system that serves thousands of deployments - but we know we want to step back and give it a big new push, letting go of some things that are no longer so important, and embracing a range of new priorities. This role is the critical engineering leadership role for that mission.

Today we use Python, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, HAProxy, and have a ReactJS front end. In other web services projects we use more Golang these days. Our next wave of Landscape engineering is an opportunity to raise the bar on SAAS and on-prem solution technologies, architectures, patterns and operations. Our goal is to make it easy for enterprises to own a few Landscape instances that serve their global estate, and to be able to apply policy and know intuitively where they stand - globally - in a very complex world of mixed Ubuntu versions, substrates and flavours.

About the role:

We are seeking a highly skilled intern with a strong programming background and an interest in engineering simulation to help automate repetitive CFD activities across the Turbomachinery Fluidic Design Team and the Fluidic Analysis Team.

The role will focus on developing robust, reusable workflows for meshing, simulation setup and launching, data extraction, post-processing, and standardized reporting, with particular emphasis on Cadence and Ansys Fluent environments. The internship is intended to reduce manual effort, improve repeatability, and shorten analysis turnaround time across the Fluidics Department.

The intern will work with engineers from both teams to identify high-value automation opportunities, translate existing engineering practices into scripts and workflows, and validate the resulting tools on representative analysis cases. Prior expertise in Cadence or Ansys Fluent is not required; strong programming ability and a willingness to learn the relevant engineering applications are more important.

Key Responsibilities:

About the role

Agent Security's mission is to safely increase how much of the world's work agents can do, starting inside Anthropic.

Claude now writes and ships code, runs experiments and acts on people's behalf, for hours at a time. How much more it can take on depends on how safely it can operate. If, in the worst case, an agent misbehaves, Anthropic and the public may bear the consequences. Our mandate is to mitigate this risk, and Anthropic’s mission depends on it.

The Partnerships team pairs security engineers with the teams at Anthropic that build Claude, build agents and rely on agents. Those teams are our partners. When a team wants its agents to do more, we threat model the plan with them and build the controls together. Most of this has no playbook, so we have often created new controls from first principles. The ones that work become part of our toolbox, spread to other teams, and in some cases ship in our products.

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead this team of security engineers. This is first and foremost a people leadership role. Few have secured agents at scale, especially at a frontier lab, so we don't expect you to have done it. We do expect you to have led security engineering teams, and we care most about how you lead people and reason about security.

This role operates at the frontier. Each model generation, and each new harness, brings new challenges. The number of teams building on agents keeps growing, and partner teams won't always agree with your calls. jobs.title: Manager Architect Cloud - Paris
jobs.description:
Présentation du poste :

Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.

Tout le reste, ce sont les ambitions fonctionnelles et techniques du client, son cadre réglementaire, son budget, les compétences qu'il peut réellement mobiliser en interne, la gouvernance qu'il veut installer, et un écosystème d'éditeurs qui gravite autour de lui. Votre rôle est de trouver le point d'équilibre entre ces forces, de le faire accepter, puis de le réajuster dès que l'une d'elles bouge.

Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.

Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT compre

jobs.title: CDI - Manager Platform Engineer - Paris

  1. Vous avez construit et exploité de l’infrastructure cloud sur Google Cloud, Azure ou AWS, en infrastructure as code.

jobs.title: Manager Cloud Architect - Paris
jobs.description:
Présentation du poste :

Concevoir une architecture d’IA, c’est engager une entreprise pour plusieurs années : l’emplacement des données, la gestion des accès, la manière dont un agent passe en production sous le regard des équipes de sécurité. Ces choix structurants, vous les construisez avec nos clients.

Tout le reste, ce sont les ambitions fonctionnelles et techniques du client, son cadre réglementaire, son budget, les compétences qu'il peut réellement mobiliser en interne, la gouvernance qu'il veut installer, et un écosystème d'éditeurs qui gravite autour de lui. Votre rôle est de trouver le point d'équilibre entre ces forces, de le faire accepter, puis de le réajuster dès que l'une d'elles bouge.

Votre point de départ n’est pas la technologie, mais l’ambition métier. Vous la traduisez en une plateforme data ou agentique pensée pour s’intégrer au système d’information existant, avec son histoire, ses contraintes et ses équipes. Votre rôle ne s’arrête pas à la validation du schéma cible : vous accompagnez les équipes de delivery jusqu’à la mise en production.

À titre d’exemple, chez l’un de nos clients, chaque nouvel agent repose désormais sur une plateforme commune qui gère nativement les droits d’accès, le monitoring et les coûts. Chaque cas d’usage s’appuie ainsi sur les fondations posées pour les précédents.

Ce poste s’adresse à vous si vous aimez embrasser un système dans son ensemble, prendre les décisions qui engagent et en expliquer les raisons.

Artefact est le partenaire de confiance des plus grandes entreprises mondiales pour déployer l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, vous rejoignez le département Engineering (environ 300 personnes, sous la responsabilité du CTO), au sein du chapter AI Architect.

Activités et responsabilités :

Sur un projet, vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les AI Applied Engineers, qui construisent et font tourner ce que vous concevez, et avec les AI Product Managers, qui portent le produit avec le client.

Côté client, deux publics sont à convaincre : les directions métier, avec lesquelles vous définissez la cible, et les équipes IT, sécurité, réseau et exploitation, sans l’adhésion desquelles rien ne passe en production. Une architecture qu’elles n’ont pas validée ne dépasse pas le stade du document. Vous êtes aussi l'interlocuteur des achats, de la conformité et des éditeurs qui veulent se positionner.

Au sein du chapter, vous relisez les designs de vos pairs, contribuez à faire grandir les architectes et les profils d’ingénierie qui vous entourent, et mettez en commun ce qui fonctionne. Vous travaillez également avec nos partenaires technologiques et les autres équipes d’Artefact.

Vos responsabilités :

  • Traduire les objectifs, les contraintes et les délais du client en une architecture que le métier comme l’IT compre

Whoever builds the leading intelligence for finance will create far more than returns. Poesis is the AI-native investment firm running autonomous agents that predict markets, construct portfolios, and manage risk. Our founders managed institutional capital at Capital Group ($3T AUM) and led enterprise ML at Goldman Sachs and Amazon. We're building a new type of firm, where live capital is the training ground for an intelligence that compounds with every signal.

About the Role

Financial markets offer something rare in AI research: a continuous, objective feedback loop where you can test new ideas, measure whether they actually work, and use real-world outcomes to inform what you build next. It’s an opportunity to do frontier research with a direct line between the ideas you explore and their real-world performance. As Head of AI, you’ll lead Poesis’s AI strategy and research, setting the technical direction for how we apply frontier AI to investing. You’ll explore new AI approaches, tackle difficult research problems and help define how we use AI to better understand and predict financial markets. This is a hands-on leadership role where you’ll set the research agenda while continuing to work directly on technical challenges.

Challenges You’ll Work On

Set Poesis’s AI research direction, identify the hardest problems worth solving and guide the team's technical work.

Push the capabilities of foundation models, agentic systems and world models through new architectures and research approaches.

Explore pre-training, mid-training and post-training methods to improve how models learn, reason and adapt.

Advance tabular ML research, including emerging methods such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs).

Tackle the challenges of learning from small, high-dimensional datasets where traditional ML methods struggle.

Turn promising research into models and systems that can solve difficult real-world problems.

About You

You’ve done exceptional AI research at a frontier AI lab, leading research initiatives and helping set technical direction.

You have deep expertise in modern AI architectures, model training and machine learning.

You have a strong research track record, including relevant publications.

You have strong mathematical and statistical foundations and know how to tackle difficult problems with limited, complex data.

You’re a hands-on technical leader who can guide other researchers while developing, testing and implementing your own ideas.

Experience with frontier tabular ML methods.

Experience applying ML to financial markets or complex, high-dimensional datasets.

Hybrid, 3 days per week on-site at our office in Menlo Park, CA, London, or Zurich. Relocation allowance available.

Competitive cash compensation commensurate with experience, plus equity and carry (share of fund profits).

Benefits

We offer excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage, alongside a strong benefits pack

Product Design Director - Patient (x/f/m)

The opportunity

Doctolib is a mission-driven healthcare technology company, founded in Paris in 2013. Today, nearly  3,000 people  work across Europe to transform the way healthcare is delivered and experienced.  More than  500,000 healthcare professionals  use Doctolib’s solutions, and the patient app is used by approximately  90 million people  across Europe.  For patients, Doctolib began as a simple way to find a healthcare professional and book an appointment. We are now building something much more ambitious: an  AI-powered Health Companion  that helps people navigate care, understand their health and take the right next step throughout their health journey.  This means moving beyond a primarily transactional product towards an experience that supports patients before, during and after care, through access to care, health information, patient data, messaging, recommendations, care plans and AI-powered assistance.  We are looking for a Product Design Director to help define what this next generation of patient experience should look and feel like.

What you will build and lead

As  Product Design Director, Patient , you will own the design vision and quality bar for Doctolib’s patient experience. You will report to our VP Design and work closely with the Product, Engineering, Medical, Data and Business leadership teams.

Your scope will cover the full patient journey, including:

access to care, search and booking;

patient messaging and teleconsultation;

the Patient Health Record and patient context;

the app homepage and daily health experience;

health content and prevention;

recommendations, reminders and care plans;

new patient services and subscription experiences;

conversational and AI-powered experiences.

The current team includes  six Senior Product Designers and one Senior Content Designer . You will lead, coach and develop this team while shaping the organisation and operating model needed to support the next phase of the Patient product.

Your mandate

You will:

Define and drive the design vision for the Patient stream, from a high-traffic booking experience to a trusted Health Companion used throughout the health journey.

Bridge two equally important challenges: continuing to improve the core access-to-care experience while creating new reasons for patients to return beyond booking.

Raise the quality bar for product design, interaction design and content across the patient experience.

Stay close enough to the product and the craft to make high-quality design decisions, not only set direction from a distance.

Shape AI-native experiences that are clear, useful and trustworthy, including recommendations, conversational interfaces and next-best actions.

Establish strong design principles for transparency, explainability, uncertainty, user control and safe escalation in a healthcare context.

Founded in 2013, Doctolib is Europe's leading AI and digital health company, serving 580,000 health professionals and 100 million people. We are building a new way to build software: agents doing the grunt work of writing, testing, reviewing and merging code, with engineers moving into a control-tower role to monitor and intervene.

Your mission: build the tooling and workflows that let AI agents and the engineers who work alongside them  test, review, ship and monitor code reliably, so Doctolib can multiply its engineering output while keeping quality and control.

The role

We're looking for a  Director of AI Developer Experience  to lead our new  AI Developer Experience  team, reporting to the VP Platform Engineering. You will also own the existing CI and Developer Experience scope.  Doctolib is moving AI adoption from a temporary SWAT team to a permanent capability. The current team includes two Product Managers and two engineers, with more people joining through internal transfers and hiring.

Your team will own:

The agent-native testing and feedback infrastructure that lets agents know, within their own workflow, whether what they built is correct.

CI/CD and build systems for the monolith and satellite services, elevated from a CI-run team into an efficient agent-testing capability.

Developer productivity measurement in the AI era DORA, autonomous change rate and complementary indicators.

The inner-loop experience: local and remote environments, onboarding, editor integration and sandboxing.

Your impact

Your responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Build the tools and workflows that  allow agents to write, test, review and merge code, including evaluation, security checks and controls  giving agents a fast, reliable feedback loop on whether what they build is correct.

Own testing and feedback for the monolith and satellite services,  elevating the current CI setup from a CI-run team into an efficient agent-testing capability.

Own developer productivity measurement  in the context of AI DORA, autonomous change rate and complementary indicators  and make it visible and actionable to feature teams.

Lead the inner-loop experience:  local and remote environments, onboarding, editor integration and sandboxing.

Build and organise the team,  developing agentic skills internally where needed, as AI adoption shifts from a temporary SWAT team to a permanent one.

Partner with Product Engineering and Product Management to understand internal users and drive adoption.

Your team

Reporting to the VP Platform Engineering,  Mike Aidane , you'll join the Platform Engineering leadership team alongside directors and senior EMs for Application Platform, Data Services and Platform Services.

You will lead the new AI Developer Experience team, which includes Automation Platform (CI team), ILOT (Internal LLMs Ops & Training team) and TestingOps.

You'll partner closely with Product Engineering, Product Management, Release Engi

We're looking for a Localization Operations Manager to audit and redesign how we conduct translation and localization end to end; from content creation, through engineering delivery, to linguistic quality review. Audit the current end-to-end localization and translation workflow for our three main markets, from source content definition through engineering execution to linguistic QA, defining and implementing improvements for an updated localization process.

jobs.title: Gaming Threat Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
WHAT MAKES US EPIC?

At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.

Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

INFOSEC

What We Do

Keep Epic’s networks, hardware, and people safe from security risks. Install security measures and operate software to protect systems and information infrastructure, including firewalls and encryption programs. Document issues as they arise and assess & report any impact caused.

What You'll Do

We're seeking a Gaming Threat Intelligence Analyst to identify, investigate, and disrupt the people who cheat, defraud, or abuse Epic's games and players. You'll track cheat developers, account sellers, and fraud operations back to the people and infrastructure behind them, then work with Ecosystem Security and Legal to turn that research into mitigations, enforcement, and legal action. This role owns investigations from first lead to finished report with minimal oversight.

In this role, you will

  • Investigate cheat developers, sellers and resellers, account sellers, tournament cheaters, DDoS providers, and exploit developers targeting Epic's games
  • Identify the people, networks, and infrastructure behind cheat products and fraud schemes, not only the products themselves
  • Investigate fraud and abuse across the ecosystem, including V-Bucks fraud, Support-A-Creator fraud, and map payout fraud
  • Monitor cheat communities and underground markets for new features, techniques, and trends, and feed findings into technical mitigations and enforcement decisions
  • Track account compromise methods and social programming tactics used against players
  • Research and maintain Epic's gaming threat landscape, including the leading threat actors, their methods, and where they are likely to move next
  • Prioritize actors by impact and build evidence packages that support takedowns, payment disruption, and litigation, and support Legal throughout the legal process
  • Work with external intel partners on reporting, cheat testing, and attribution, and exchange intelligence with gaming industry peers
  • Support incident response with research on cheats, exploits, compromised accounts, and leaks
  • Write case reports and contribute to quarterly threat reporting, and own small projects from the team backlog end to end

As a Principal ML Engineer on Matchmaking, you’ll own the technical vision and execution for the models, objective functions, and algorithms that make those decisions. You’ll combine predictions of high-value player actions with optimization of player and developer utility and system efficiency, serving millions of players across hundreds of thousands of servers in global datacenters.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Distributed Storage & AI Infrastructure
jobs.description:
About the Role

In this role, you will operate, scale, and optimize multi-petabyte storage systems purpose-built for the world’s largest AI training and inference workloads. Storage now sits on the inference critical path as well, so you’ll also build the caching and data-movement layers that deliver KV cache and model weights directly into GPU memory at fabric speed. You’ll manage and scale high-performance parallel filesystems and object stores, evaluate and integrate cutting-edge technologies such as Vast, Weka, Ceph, and Lustre, and solve the complex engineering challenges of operating at extreme throughput, low-latency data paths, and massive cluster-scale storage operations.

You will also build Kubernetes-native storage operators and self-service platforms that provide automated provisioning, strict multi-tenancy, performance isolation, and quota enforcement at cluster scale. Day-to-day, you’ll optimize end-to-end data paths for 10-50 GB/s per node, design multi-tier caching architectures, implement intelligent prefetching and model-weight distribution, build KV-cache offload and reuse tiers for inference, and tune parallel filesystems for AI workloads.

Responsibilities

  • Architect and implement the technical strategy and storage roadmap for Together AI, driving high-performance architectural decisions as we scale our GPU fleet.
  • Engineer and scale multi-petabyte AI/ML storage systems by integrating Vast, Weka, and Ceph while executing deep cost optimization through automated tiering and lifecycle policies.
  • Develop intelligent caching and tiered storage architectures to achieve extreme IOPS and cluster-wide throughput at GPU scale for training and inference workloads, including GPU-direct (RDMA) delivery of model weights for fast cold starts and autoscaling.
  • Design and build KV-cache offload and reuse for inference: tiering KV blocks across GPU HBM, host memory, local NVMe, and distributed cache, enabling prefix reuse across requests and nodes, and integrating with inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) to cut time-to-first-token.
  • Tune storage isolation at the L2/L3 network layers to ensure secure, production-grade multi-tenancy for storage clients.
  • Code Kubernetes storage operators and controllers to enable automated provisioning, self-service abstractions, and quota enforcement.
  • Engineer end-to-end data paths to achieve 10+ GB/s per GPU node; architect multi-tier caching for model weights, KV cache, and datasets; tune parallel filesystems using advanced profiling; and scale storage infrastructure across thousands of nodes.
  • Optimize end-to-end data paths through advanced benchmarking and profiling, contributing high-impact code to open-source storage and inference projects and internal tooling.

Requirements

Waste is high, margins are thin, and most distributor order processes are done over the phone, tracked across broad spreadsheets, and based on intuition rather than strong data.

At Choco, we’re changing that. We build software used daily by food distributors and their customers to run their business. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

We are hiring an Engineering Manager/Tech Lead Manager to lead the team that runs Kubernetes on bare-metal GPU infrastructure at Together AI. You will own how thousands of GPUs across our data centers are provisioned, orchestrated and kept healthy for the customers training, fine-tuning and serving models on our platform.

Together AI is the AI Native Cloud: a full-stack platform for running open and custom generative AI models, from GPU clusters to serverless inference. Our research and engineering teams contribute widely used open-source work such as FlashAttention, and our infrastructure runs at the frontier of GPU hardware.

This team sits at the base of that stack. Every training run, inference endpoint and customer cluster depends on the reliability, utilization and speed of the bare-metal Kubernetes layer you will lead.

Responsibilities

Own the bare-metal Kubernetes platform

  • Set the technical direction for how we run Kubernetes on bare metal across multiple data centers and regions.

  • Work with data center operations, networking, hardware vendors, inference, training and product teams to plan capacity and launch new hardware generations.
  • Represent the platform's needs and trade-offs to leadership, and turn customer requirements into a clear roadmap.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in infrastructure, SRE or platform engineering, including 2+ years managing engineers.

At Scopely, we create games for everyone - and want to ensure that the people behind our games reflect that! The Technical Release Manager will own the complete path from local changes to validated availability across all development lanes. You will set the technical strategy and operating model for how hundreds of contributors safely exchange changes while maintaining velocity. What You’ll Do

  • Own the path from local work to validated availability, including branch strategy, merge policy, propagation, validation, and exception handling across all development lanes
  • Set the lifecycle contract for each development lane: why it exists, what belongs there, how it stays synchronized, conflict resolution, and retirement criteria
  • Design and implement the technical systems and policies that enable change management at scale across source control, CI/CD, validation, and release infrastructure
  • Surface dependencies and potential integration collisions early enough for teams to sequence work or knowingly accept rework, then preserve ordering and context as changes move between lanes

  • Measure flow health metrics and turn incidents and proven manual practices into better policy, tooling, and operations
  • Coordinate work across Developer Experience, QA, CI/build infrastructure, production operations, and domain teams, with clear owners and backup coverage for critical operations
  • Mentor and develop junior team members in release engineering and infrastructure practices

What We’re Looking For

  • Highly experienced hands-on engineer with a track record of technical leadership on cross-functional programs

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Real-Time Video Generation
jobs.description:
About Cantina

Cantina Labs  is a social AI company, developing a suite of advanced real-time models that push the boundaries of expression, personality, and realism. We bring characters to life, transforming how people tell stories, connect, and create. We build and power ecosystems. Cantina, our flagship social AI platform, is just the beginning.

If you're excited about the potential AI has to shape human creativity and social interactions, join us in building the future!

About the Role

We’re working on real-time video generation for interactive characters, spanning realistic humans, stylized characters, and non-human identities. We want these characters to feel present: to speak, react, and express themselves through their face, gestures, and body language.

This brings together a set of closely connected research problems. A character needs a consistent appearance, expressive and coherent motion, and a natural relationship between speech and movement. The model also needs to respond quickly and keep generating reliably as an interaction unfolds. Quality, controllability, and efficiency all matter.

You’ll work across streaming generation, fine-tuning, distillation, inference optimization, and data. Some problems will call for a new training approach; others will come down to better examples, a more useful evaluation, or understanding a bottleneck in the implementation. Part of the job is figuring out which intervention is worth making.

You’ll have substantial freedom to propose directions, investigate unfamiliar ideas, and shape what we work on next. We’re looking for someone who enjoys that freedom and can turn it into a steady sequence of useful experiments.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's customers renew on a mix of committed and consumption contracts, and the number of renewals is growing faster than any team of people could keep pace with. We don't want to answer that by hiring hundreds of renewal managers. We want renewals to run as a system: Claude and agents do most of the work, from spotting risk to drafting the offer to closing a standard renewal in product, and people step in where judgment, negotiation or relationships matter.

You'll design, build and run that system. You'll own the renewal outcome for the business globally and the product and technology that delivers it. You'll lead a small team of builders and the human layer, internal specialists and outsourced partners, that handles what agents can't yet. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Deal Desk, Finance, Billing and Product Engineering.

This is a Claude-first role. You'll use Claude every day to do your own work, and the renewal function will be one of the clearest examples inside Anthropic of what AI-run operations look like.

What you'll own in your first year

  • The design of the renewal system: which work agents run end to end, which work goes to a person, and the handoff rules between them.
  • A standard renewal that needs no person: a Claude-generated offer in product ahead of term end, accepted and provisioned automatically, with anything outside guidance routed to a seller with a recommended quote.
  • The data the system runs on: contract, commit burndown and usage data clean enough that agents and people trust it, built with Billing and Finance.
  • Early-warning signals for consumption risk and commitment shortfall, and what happens when one fires.
  • The human layer: how internal specialists, outsourced partners and account teams work around the agents, and the measures they're held to.
  • The next large renewal cycles, run with fewer manual steps per renewal than today.
  • Weekly renewal and retention forecasts grounded in usage and contract data.
  • Executive renewal conversations on the largest and most complex accounts, alongside account teams.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the Role:

At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative. Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.

Many of the people who could gain the most from Claude are the least able to buy it the usual way. A teacher often pays for tools out of pocket. A small nonprofit has no procurement team. A university lab that wants to use Claude has to go through funding, an IT office, and a purchasing department at once. Beneficial Deployments works to reach them, through programs like Claude for Teachers and Claude for Nonprofits and through our work with researchers.

What stands between those people and Claude is rarely the model. It's proving they qualify, getting the right price, buying in a way their institution allows, and landing in the right organization with the right permissions. Those steps run through identity, billing, provisioning, and fraud systems that were built for commercial customers. Our Access team makes them work for everyone else.

We're looking for engineers who find it deeply satisfying to remove the one thing stopping thousands of teachers or scientists from getting started. You'll work in other teams' codebases as often as our own, and much of the job is earning the trust of the engineers, accountants, and safety reviewers who own those systems. This role's focus is access. Experience with billing or identity is a big plus. What matters most is that you finish hard things that cross team lines, get the details right when money and trust are involved, and care about who is on the other end.

About the role

How do we know whether a model is safe - and how do we know whether the systems we built to catch misuse actually catch it?

Anthropic answers both questions with evaluations. We measure model behavior across misuse, prompt injection, and user well-being to inform training and deployment decisions. We also use AI to investigate potential misuse of Claude, analyzing real-world traffic to surface bad actors and emerging threats that drive enforcement actions. Neither is worth much unless the evaluations behind them are representative, robust, and trustworthy.

This role builds the methods and infrastructure that make them so. Sitting at the intersection of applied ML research and engineering, you'll design experiments to improve how we evaluate both model behavior and the agentic systems that govern it, build datasets that represent real abuse rather than clean approximations of it, and ship those methods into the pipelines that gate model training, agent changes, and launch decisions.

Responsibilities

Evaluation research and methodology. Design and run experiments to improve evaluation quality — developing methods to generate representative test data, simulate realistic user behavior, and validate grading accuracy. Research how different factors (multi-turn conversations, tools, long context, user diversity) impact model safety behavior. Analyze evaluation coverage to identify measurement gaps, and evolve evals so they remain unsaturated and high-signal as model and agent capabilities advance.

Agentic investigation evals. Build and own the evaluation harness for an agentic investigation system — defining metrics, test cases, and grading approaches for a complex, long-horizon agent. Measure agent performance end-to-end (detection precision and recall, investigation quality, robustness) and drive hill-climbing on the hardest harm areas. Construct RL environments to improve Claude's safety investigation capabilities.

Datasets grounded in real harm. Construct high-quality eval datasets representing real-world misuse across harm areas such as cyber attacks, bio weapons, and influence operations, drawing from both real traffic patterns and synthetic generation. jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Performance Marketing Manager, Forecasting & Market Intelligence, to join our Performance Marketing team in Canada on a remote basis.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day, whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers developing, publishing, and innovating across the games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

The Performance Marketing team helps drive sustainable player growth across Scopely’s portfolio. This role will sit at the intersection of performance marketing, forecasting, competitive intelligence, and market research, supporting active and upcoming Slate titles as they move from early planning through testing, soft launch, and global launch.

What You Will Do

You will build the analytical foundation behind UA forecasts and growth plans: identifying the right comparable titles, developing market and geo assumptions, maintaining benchmarks, tracking competitive signals, and turning incomplete information into structured first-pass recommendations. This is a highly analytical role for someone who enjoys working through ambiguity and can challenge, validate, and refine assumptions rather than taking inputs at face value.

  • Develop first-pass performance marketing forecasts and supporting inputs for upcoming Slate titles, including install curves, geo-tier views, channel assumptions, paid and organic assumptions, and launch phasing.
  • Build and maintain relevant comparable game-peer sets based on genre, monetization model, platform, geo mix, audience, launch strategy, creative approach, and expected scale.
  • Develop and maintain dCPI benchmarks and degradation curves, combining Scopely historical performance, partner benchmarks, competitor data, and external market signals.
  • Support organic forecasting by developing assumptions around baseline organic demand, paid-driven lift, launch/IP halo, virality, and organic-to-paid ratios.
  • Build sensitivity analyses that make the impact of key assumptions clear and help teams understand the range of potential outcomes.
  • Track competitor UA investment, creative trends, app-store movement, channel activity, launch performance, and regional signals across relevant games and genres.
  • Produce recurring market-intelligence and competitive-pulse readouts that identify meaningful changes in the market and potential implications for Slate titles.
  • Incorporate learnings from market research, beta acquisition, creative and audience testing, soft launch, and other pre-launch signals into forecast assumptions.
  • Support regional opportunity sizing and geo strategy, including differences in acquisition cost, scale, organic potential, and market dynamics

Fastned owns and operates a network of 400+ fast charging stations across 10 European countries, allowing electric vehicle drivers to charge their car with 100% green energy in just 15 minutes. Our goal is a European network of 1000 fast charging stations in prime locations, where all electric vehicles can charge with renewable energy from the sun and wind. We have recently been voted best charging network in the UK, France and the Netherlands. If you want to make a difference and work in an informal, international scale-up environment with future prospects, then read on!

Your role

Fastned aims to accelerate the transition towards sustainable mobility by giving fast charging to electric drivers. Part of that mission is making car charging as simple as charging your phone, and paying for it should be just as effortless. As a Backend Engineer in the Payments team, you will help make paying for a charge frictionless, secure and reliable. Drivers can pay through the Fastned app, by QR code or with a contactless card at the charger.

The team owns Fastned’s payments domain end to end. That covers integrations with payment service providers and payment terminals. It also covers the services behind payment methods, wallets, pre-authorisation and session payments, billing, invoicing and dunning. .

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Bioinformatics
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Senior Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Graphics
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Graphics Engineer. This role can be based remotely in the UK, Ireland, Portugal, Spain or from our Barcelona hub on a hybrid basis. If you're open to working in any of these locations, there's no need to apply more than once. We'll discuss location preferences during the hiring process. We can support with visa sponsorship from any location.

We are looking for strong rendering expertise and a passion for delivering high-quality, high-performance visuals. You will work on real-time rendering features and optimizations that help our game look and run its best across a wide range of devices.

We are in the early stages of development on an ambitious, unannounced, cross-platform Strategy/MMO title, creating a team of talented and passionate game makers to join us on this exciting journey!

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play, every day — whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing, and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

What You Will Do

  • Develop and optimize real-time rendering features on mobile platforms using Vulkan (Android) and Metal (iOS).

  • Work with clustered/meshlet-based geometry systems, implementing GPU-driven visibility, culling, and LOD.

  • Integrate and refine modern rendering techniques such as clustered/tiled lighting, temporal anti-aliasing (TAA), and super-resolution (TSR).

  • Assist in the development of real-time global illumination features in collaboration with senior technical staff, ensuring scalability across different device tiers.

  • Write and optimize shaders (HLSL/GLSL/MSL) for power-efficient mobile performance.

  • Profile GPU/CPU performance and analyze rendering bottlenecks using tools like RenderDoc, Perfetto, Xcode GPU Debugger, and Mali/Snapdragon profilers.

  • Contribute to GPU memory layout design, draw submission strategies, and render pass optimizations for tile-based GPUs.

  • Collaborate closely with engine and content teams to ensure visuals meet quality and performance goals across platforms.

  • Stay informed on industry rendering trends and suggest improvements to our pipeline.

What We Are Looking For

  • 5+ years of graphics programming experience, with a focus on mobile platforms.

  • Strong C++ skills with experience working in performance-critical rendering code.

  • Solid knowledge of Vulkan and/or Metal APIs.

  • Experience with Unity’s Scriptable Render Pipeline (SRP), including extending or customizing SRPs.

jobs.title: Research Scientist, AI Safety and Alignment
jobs.description:
Scale Labs, Research Scientist — AI Safety and Alignment

As the leading data and evaluation partner for frontier AI companies, Scale plays a central role in understanding and safeguarding AI systems. Building on this expertise, Scale Labs has launched a new team focused on technical AI safety and policy research, to bridge the gap between frontier AI research and policy, helping policymakers make informed, evidence-based decisions about AI capabilities and risks.

Our research tackles some of the hardest open problems in AI safety: assessing the alignment of frontier models, developing control protocols and monitoring methods, preserving the monitorability, understanding failure modes in multi-agent systems and recursive self-improvement. We collaborate closely with partners across industry, the public sector, and academia and regularly publish our findings. We are looking for talented researchers to join us in shaping this vision.

As a Research Scientist on this team, you will conduct research and build evaluations, tools, and datasets that help us understand and reduce risks from frontier AI systems. For example, you might do any or all of the following:

  • Design and stress-test control protocols and monitoring systems that detect and limit unsafe behavior by AI models and agents in deployment;
  • Build alignment evaluations that probe for deception, sabotage, scheming, reward hacking, and other misaligned behaviors;
  • Study monitorability, including whether a model’s reasoning stays faithful and legible enough to supervise, and how training methods and deployment practices can preserve or erode it;
  • Investigate risks that emerge when multiple AI agents interact, such as collusion, coordination failures and steerability;
  • Develop threat models and evaluations for AI systems that automate AI research and development, to track progress toward recursive self-improvement and inform preparedness planning;
  • Work with government agencies and other labs to scope and design evaluations that measure and mitigate risks from advanced AI;
  • Publish research and evaluation methodologies, and write technical reports for policymakers.

Ideally you’d have:

  • Commitment to our mission of promoting safe, secure, and trustworthy AI as capabilities continue to advance.
  • Practical experience conducting technical research collaboratively. You should be comfortable building and instrumenting ML pipelines, building evaluation harnesses, running experiments on frontier models and agents, and quickly turning new ideas from the research literature into working prototypes.
  • Familiarity with current research in at least one of the areas above.
  • A track record of published research in machine learning, particularly in AI safety and alignment.
  • At least three year

jobs.title: Product Frontend Engineer
jobs.description:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app.

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.

Where this is going

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.

Why this role exists

Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next  is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Anthropic has done pioneering work examining the economic impacts of AI. The AI & Rule of Law team takes an analogous approach to a different question: how will AI affect our constitutional democratic institutions?

Increasingly powerful AI systems will put pressure on societal functions at every level — the courts, legislatures, electoral systems, oversight bodies, and the legal frameworks that hold democratic governance together. Our team exists to ask hard questions about those vulnerabilities, and to seek out strategies for protecting democratic freedoms — in the short and long term, through both technical and policy levers.

We are looking for someone with deep expertise in both AI and at least one of: government, political science, or public policy. jobs.title: Product Engineer, Shop
jobs.description:
ABOUT INSIFY

We sell a mix of insurance products to small businesses (SME's) in the Netherlands, Germany and France, and we are in the process of scaling into more markets.

Insurance infrastructure is brutal to get right. Every carrier has its own spec, every product its own underwriting rules, every country its own regulatory requirements. Most insurers throw people and process at that complexity - one-off integrations, workarounds on workarounds. We're building it differently: our insurance platform is where we consolidate that complexity, so that launching a new product or market becomes a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by more than €40M from investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

About the role

You would join the Shop team, responsible for everything that happens after a small business buys a policy from us. You would help shape how the platform handles the next product and the next country, on a system already carrying live policies and real customers.

The team owns end-to-end policy lifecycle management (mid-term adjustments, automated renewals, cancellations, and payment flows) alongside the backoffice tooling that gives our operations and support teams full visibility and control. We work closely with the Claims Team, and with the Activation Teams that turn a lead into a paying customer. Product and engineering together are 30+ people.

Every country has its own regulatory quirks, and every insurance product has unique data structures, lifecycle rules, and money flows.

As we expand across Europe, our goal isn't to write custom glue code for every new launch. It's to design elegant, reusable platform abstractions. We're building a system where introducing a new country or product feels like snapping modular building blocks together.

You're joining at an exciting inflection point: we have real traction, proven scale, and you get to directly build the foundational platform that powers our next wave of European growth.

What you'll be doing

Owning end-to-end the discovery and delivery of crucial platform features that enable our ability to scale as an insurance business

Continuously and relentlessly seeking opportunities to turn new product demands into platform capabilities and features that scale across countries and insurance product lines

Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others

What you'll need

3+ years building complex web applications and services, with real production ownership

Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your direct stack to get to results, be that data / backend / frontend

You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt
